(iv) P4 + limited dry Cl2 → PCl3 (phosphorus trichloride). Central phosphorus in PCl3 has three Cl and one lone pair; geometry is trigonal pyramidal (like NH3).
(v) Ca3P2 + H2O (hydrolysis) → H3PO2 (or PH3 + H3PO4?). The phosphorus in H3PO2 (phosphorous acid) has three ligands (two O and one H) and one lone pair; geometry is trigonal pyramidal.
(vi) NH4+ + NaOH (warm) → NH3 (ammonia). Nitrogen in NH3 has three H and one lone pair; geometry is trigonal pyramidal.
(vii) P4S10 + H2O (hydrolysis) → H2PSO4 (or P4O10 + H2O?). The phosphorus in the resulting acid (H2PSO4) typically adopts tetrahedral geometry with four substituents and no lone pair; not trigonal pyramidal.
Thus reactions with trigonal pyramidal geometry around the named element: (ii), (iv), (v), (vi) → 4 reactions.
Answer integer 4.
